title: CEO Interview with Peter Jenkins of Infinitesima
gist: Infinitesima CEO Peter Jenkins (27-28 years at ASML) pitches the Metron3D, a laser-driven hybrid optical/AFM Rapid Probe Microscope that gives non-destructive, in-line 3D angstrom-scale metrology at production throughput. Hybrid bonding for advanced packaging/HBM is its strongest beachhead, with SK hynix qualification, an imec program and a Multiprobe roadmap.

insights.claim: As device structures approach atomic dimensions, incumbent metrology is breaking down: optical scatterometry needs a model rebuilt for every structure/process change and misses local variability, CD-SEM cannot measure in 3D and is running out of contrast, and TEM is destructive and takes days.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Process-control gap at leading nodes creates room for new metrology entrants and techniques.
insights.quote: CD-SEM cannot measure in 3D and is running out of contrast.

insights.claim: Customers say process learning cycles are held back by metrology that is too slow, indirect or destructive; building OCD models and getting volume TEM can take weeks.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Metrology speed is a bottleneck on yield ramp, a lever for fab time-to-volume.
insights.quote: Building OCD models and getting volume TEM can take weeks.
insights.locator: What keeps your customers up at night?

insights.claim: AI is pushing the industry to bring new processes to volume faster than ever, so faster direct metrology that shortens development cycles and yield ramp gains value.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: AI-driven node/packaging cadence lifts demand for process-control tools.
insights.quote: AI is pushing the industry to bring new processes to volume faster than ever before

insights.claim: Infinitesima's Rapid Probe Microscope is a high-speed hybrid optical/AFM deployed as the fully automated in-line Metron3D, measuring structures directly and non-destructively in 3D with ~0.2 nm lateral pixel resolution (about one silicon atom).
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Brings AFM, historically a lab/reference tool, into production lines.
insights.quote: with a lateral pixel resolution of approximately 0.2 nm, which is about the size of a single silicon atom

insights.claim: Conventional AFM is accurate but slow and scaling it means adding multiple heads that must be matched; Infinitesima instead drives the probe with a laser rather than a piezo actuator and tracks tip position in 3 axes with an interferometer, gaining speed without multi-head matching cost and complexity.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Differentiation rests on optical actuation as the throughput unlock vs multi-head AFM rivals.
insights.quote: drives the probe with a laser rather than a piezo actuator, and tracks the tip position in 3-axis with an interferometer
insights.locator: What does the competitive landscape look like

insights.claim: AFM, together with TEM, is accepted by the industry as a ground-truth reference technique; its historic limitation has been speed, not trust.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: If speed is solved, AFM-based tools inherit reference-grade credibility in production.
insights.quote: together with TEM it is a ground truth technique the industry trusts
insights.locator: Atomic force microscopy has long been accepted

insights.claim: Infinitesima's strongest application is hybrid bonding for advanced packaging, HBM and heterogeneous integration, especially copper pad recess and dishing measurement.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Advanced packaging/HBM growth is the primary demand driver for this metrology niche.
insights.quote: Copper pad recess and dishing is where direct 3D measurement wins most clearly.
insights.locator: What application areas are your strongest?

insights.claim: In hybrid bonding a bonding error commits two finished wafers at once with no chance to rework, raising the cost of undetected excursions and the value of pre-bond geometry measurement.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Higher scrap cost per error in packaging boosts willingness to pay for inspection/metrology.
insights.quote: A bonding error commits two finished wafers at once, with no chance to rework
insights.locator: What application areas are your strongest?

insights.claim: One Metron3D system covers die-by-die measurement, long-range profiling and large-area scanning, tasks customers typically address today with several separate tools.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Tool consolidation pitch could displace multiple incumbent metrology tools per step.
insights.locator: What application areas are your strongest?

insights.claim: Infinitesima plans to expand into CMP flatness, EUV resist metrology as High-NA ramps, and post-etch 3D metrology; a three-year imec program targets hybrid wafer bonding, High-NA EUV and CFET.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Ties the company's TAM to High-NA EUV and CFET adoption timelines.
insights.quote: Our three-year programme with imec is focused on these challenging new processes, Hybrid Wafer Bonding, High NA EUV, and CFET transistor structures.
insights.locator: What application areas are your strongest?

insights.claim: Infinitesima is developing Multiprobe, scanning with many probes in parallel so throughput scales with probe count; enabling sub-systems (parallel interferometric detection, multi-lever probe arrays) are demonstrated, targeting full-die nanometre metrology in minutes rather than hours.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Would push AFM-class metrology from sampling to full-die coverage.
insights.quote: full die metrology at nanometre scale in measurement times of minutes not hours
insights.locator: What new features/technology are you working on?

insights.claim: Infinitesima has 140+ staff and works with SK hynix, imec and ASML; SK hynix put Metron3D through a rigorous in-fab evaluation that demonstrated it meets high-volume manufacturing requirements.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: SK hynix (HBM leader) validation is a key commercial proof point for a private UK metrology firm.

insights.claim: Metrology tools, once qualified into a process, are very rarely changed, making qualification slow and multi-step but creating durable incumbency.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Design-in wins in metrology are sticky; early qualifications compound into recurring revenue.
insights.quote: Once a metrology tool is qualified into a process, it is very rarely changed, so trust matters enormously.

insights.claim: Jenkins says his ASML tenure gave visibility into lithography roadmaps aligned across multiple future nodes, which revealed an emerging need for new 3D process-control solutions.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Signals ex-ASML talent sees 3D metrology as an under-served roadmap need.
insights.locator: What drew you from ASML to Infinitesima?
